sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Python syntax questions are the gatekeeping round of every fresher interview. Interviewers ask them to verify you can write real Python — not pseudocode. Pass this round and the conversation opens up. Fail it and the rest of your preparation doesn't matter.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Think in **three layers**:

1. **Values** — everything is an object; types determine what operations are valid.
2. **Binding** — variables are names bound to objects, not typed boxes.
3. **Scope** — LEGB: Local → Enclosing → Global → Built-in. This single rule explains 90% of NameError surprises.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Mutable vs immutable** — list/dict/set are mutable; int/str/tuple/frozenset are not. Mutation through a function parameter is the most common gotcha.
- **`is` vs `==`** — `is` tests identity (same object in memory), `==` tests equality (same value). The only safe `is` uses are `is None` and `is True/False`.
- **LEGB scope rule** — name lookup order. The `global` and `nonlocal` keywords override it.
- **String formatting** — f-strings are the modern answer (Python 3.6+). Know `.format()` for legacy code.
- **`pass`, `break`, `continue`** — all three appear in fresher screens; know the precise difference.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the difference between `is` and `==`?'** — mention integer caching (-5 to 256) as the gotcha where `is` sometimes returns True for integers.
- **'What is a mutable default argument problem?'** — `def f(lst=[])` accumulates across calls. Fix: use `None` as default.
- **'Explain the LEGB rule'** — have a 30-second example ready.
- **'What data types are immutable in Python?'** — int, float, str, bool, tuple, frozenset, bytes.

sections.body: > *"In Python, X works like this — the key thing to understand is Y, and the one gotcha interviewers always probe is Z. In my college project I encountered this when [brief example]."*
